_readme: Adaptive music: one song per floor, exported as N separate stems that ALL
PLAY AT ONCE. Intensity is expressed by fading stems in and out, never by
starting or stopping them -- that is what makes drift impossible.
ADDING A FLOOR is meant to be this file plus a folder, never code:
1. Create Resources/Audio/Music/FloorN/ and drop the stems in it.
2. Copy a `sets` block, change id/folder/bpm/stems.
3. Add a line to `floors` pointing at it.
`stems` ORDER IS THE MIX ORDER AND IS AUTHORITATIVE. Every tier's numbers
are indices into it, so reordering `stems` silently re-points all four
tiers. It is the one field to change carefully.
NINE IS NOT A MAGIC NUMBER. Five stems works; twelve works. The code reads
the array length.
`gain` IS PER SET, NEVER PER STEM. A quiet pad and a loud lead are quiet
and loud on purpose -- normalising each stem individually flattens the
arrangement. Do NOT add stems to audio_levels.json. Measure the set by
rendering every stem at unity and correcting THAT figure.
All four tiers must be declared. An omitted one is refused at load rather
than inherited, because inheriting would silently play the wrong mix.
`quantiseBars` is how many bars a layer change waits for before starting.
1 is responsive; 4 or 8 is more musical but can lag by up to ~20s at 96
BPM. Per set, because the right answer depends on the song.
`stingPath` is an optional one-shot fired over the top when this set first
reaches its boss tier -- the layered replacement for the old boss intro.
STATUS: no stems have been recorded yet. floor_1 below is the PILOT SPEC,
written so the composer knows the folder name, the stem names and the tier
split before recording. Until those nine files exist the game falls back to
the old MusicTrack beds automatically and sounds exactly as it did before.
Export requirements for whoever writes the music are in
docs/handoffs/adaptive_music/README.md section 6 -- identical length,
tempo and sample rate, no head trimming, master bus bypassed.
